rejected_candidates.candidate: Theorem 1, the Oettli--Prager componentwise backward-error formula
rejected_candidates.reason: The result is explicitly quoted from Oettli and Prager (1964), and this paper supplies no proof. The close NumStability formalization is source-only and unavailable to L; asking agents to prove it would add source proof material absent from this paper.

rejected_candidates.candidate: Theorem 2, one-step iterative refinement implies componentwise stability
rejected_candidates.reason: The theorem is explicitly attributed to Skeel (1980), and the paper refers readers there for the complicated detailed conditions and proof. Although the compiled library has iterative-refinement results, selecting this theorem would violate the requirement that the paper supply the proof text.

rejected_candidates.candidate: condition formulas and comparisons (4)-(12), and split error bounds (13)-(17)
rejected_candidates.reason: These are short absolute-value, triangle-inequality, and scalar comparisons once the cited perturbation formula is accepted. They need no substantial compiled theorem and are below the T3 difficulty floor.

rejected_candidates.candidate: no-guard-digit and underflow extensions in Section 3
rejected_candidates.reason: The paper gives qualitative summaries and refers the underflow analysis to Demmel (1984); it does not provide a complete proof suitable for a source-backed task.

The matrix identity reducing the desired quantity to an infinity-norm estimate is short. Correctness of the Hager--Higham estimator is cited from earlier work, and the matching NumStability condition-estimator modules are uncompiled.
These are finite empirical executions and observations rather than difficult universally quantified theorems proved in the paper.

T1.decision: Selected the sparse-row computed-residual error bound in Section 2.2. L uses the substantial compiled conventional residual theorem once, while N reconstructs the rounded dot-product and subtraction analysis.

T2.decision: Skipped. The only plausible multi-operation theorem is Skeel's externally sourced iterative-refinement result. No result proved in this paper needs at least two distinct substantial compiled NumStability theorems.

T3.decision: Skipped. The paper's self-contained condition identities and split bounds are materially below qualifying-T2 difficulty; the harder refinement, underflow, and estimator results are quoted or summarized from earlier sources.

selection_policy: Use only mathematical conclusions whose statement and supporting derivation are present in this paper.
Do not turn Oettli--Prager or Skeel theorems quoted from earlier papers into P33 tasks.
Count the conventional residual theorem as one substantial result even though it has internal dot-product dependencies.
Do not create a T2 merely because an iterative-refinement implementation performs residuals and triangular solves.
Do not inflate short condition-number inequalities or estimator identities into T3 tasks.
Keep every public definition paper-scoped and free of NumStability imports.
Assign tiers only after comparison with the complete frozen NumStability source, its importable compiled subset, and Mathlib.
